newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PRESIDENT SIGNS DEATH PENALTY BAN INTO LAW.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PRESIDENT SIGNS DEATH PENALTY BAN INTO LAW.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski on Thursday signed into law a new criminal code abolishing the death penalty, the president's press office said in a statement.
Kwasniewski signed the bill despite widespread calls last month to restore the death penalty after several appalling murders including the torture killing of a student by a gang.

Public opinion surveys suggest most Poles support capital punishment although Justice Minister Leszek Kubicki has argued that if Poland restored executions it would not be able to ratify article six of the European Convention on Human Rights.
The death penalty had been suspended since shortly before the fall of communism in 1989 and was scrapped in the new criminal code approved by parliament last month.

"While abandoning the death penalty, the principle has been applied of strict responsiblity for actions within organised crime groups and for people who derive their regular income from committing crimes," the statement said.

"The leading idea in the new criminal code is the defense of the dignity of the person and his well-being. The catalogue of punishments enshrined in the code allows the judge to deploy a wider choice of punishments suited to specific circumstances of a crime," the statement said.
The last execution in Poland, by hanging, was carried out in 1988.
The new code, with a maximum penalty of 25 years in jail, is to take effect on January 1.
